page.layout: Running head at top centre-left: "LIB. II. Scutum Regium." Page number 87 at top right, above the narrow empty column. One text column on the right page, running from top to bottom, with a narrow empty column to its right. Signature "G 4" at the foot beside the last line. The left strip of the scan shows the edge of the neighbouring page and is not transcribed.

main_text.p: insuper in domo Cæsaris Toparscion Christianus, Antonini Cæsaris educator ; Quin & tum temporis Romani Imperij velut obsidem nobilissimam Ægypti præfecturam (Augustalem dictam) obtinuit Philippus Christianus, ordinis Equestris, quem Seuerus in Epistola ad cum missa, propter præfecturæ istius momentum & dignitatem, Regem potius quàm præfectum appellandum fatetur ; neque tamen Christiani ad Philippum tanquam belli caput confugiunt, nec Philippus eos ad arma sollicitat, licèt Ægyptij natura sua ad rebellandum procliues essent. Sed dic Sodes Tertullia-ne, Cùm nec fortitudo, nec multitudo, nec bellandi peritia, nec oratorum suadela, nec ductores vobis desint, Cur interim tanquam oues ad macellum, Ceruices iugo submittitis? & acerbissima supplicia sine querela, sine murmure toleratis? Certè te nihil aliud responsurum auguror, quàm quod ipse habes, vel in Apologetico ad Scapulam : absit ut ultionem nos aliquam machinemur, quam à Deo expectamus, vel Contra gen-tes,

page.notes: Left strip of the scan is the edge of the neighbouring page; not transcribed. Word "Toparscion" (printed Toparscion, italic): uncertain, possibly Greek-derived; read as printed. Mark over "Antonini" and over "Æ" of "Ægypti" (ornamental or ligature mark): not transcribed as text. "cum" after "ad" has a superscript mark possibly indicating a ligature; read as cum. "Cùm" accent as printed. Paragraph continues from the previous page and runs on to the bottom of the page without a new paragraph. Page 87 is the right-hand page; the narrow right column is empty.
